chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from al-ʿAmrakī ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar, from his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man: is it proper for him to insert medicine [into himself] and then perform salat (prayer) while it is still with him? Does it invalidate the wudu (ablution)? He said, “It does not invalidate the wudu (ablution), but he should not perform salat (prayer) until he expels it.”

key_terms.الْوُضُوءَ: wudu (ablution), the ritual purification before salat (prayer)
key_terms.يَسْتَدْخِلَ: to insert something into the body internally
key_terms.يَطْرَحَهُ: to cast it out or remove it
key_terms.يَنْقُضُ: to invalidate or break a state of ritual purity

ai.seo_question: Does inserted medicine invalidate wudu (ablution) or prevent salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about medicine inserted into the body and its effect on ritual purity and salat (prayer). It states that such a case does not invalidate wudu (ablution), but salat (prayer) should be delayed until the substance is removed.
